Stiefel Congruence and Spectral Rectification Compress Condition Numbers While Preserving SPD Geometry

Paper: SPDNet: A Riemannian Network for SPD Matrix Learning (AAAI 2017) · Geometry: Stiefel Congruence Projection (WXW⊤W X W^\topWXW⊤) + Spectral Rectification (ReEig) + Log-Euclidean Tangent Map (LogEig)

Can deep neural networks learn hierarchical spatial filters directly on the cone of symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices without flattening second-order sensor structure? To test whether Stiefel bilinear projections and eigenvalue rectification preserve positive definiteness while bounding spectral conditioning, we evaluate SPDNet across synthetic manifolds, 93×9393 \times 9393×93 HDM05 skeletal covariances, and cross-session BNCI2014-001 EEG recordings. First, Stiefel-parametrized BiMap(12, 8), ReEig(1e-4), and LogEig layers maintain orthogonality to 3.78e-7, clamp minimum eigenvalues at 0.0263 >= 1e-4, and output exact 36-dimensional tangent vectors (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on real 93×9393 \times 9393×93 HDM05 covariances, BiMap(93, 30) followed by ReEig compresses median condition numbers from 6.92e5 down to 1.29e5 with finite Loewner gradients (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, across our 10-seed spd-bench HDM05 harness and MOABB BNCI2014-001 cross-session evaluation, SPDNet reaches 63.10±1.5363.10 \pm 1.5363.10±1.53% on HDM05 (vs. 61.60±1.3561.60 \pm 1.3561.60±1.35% published) and 75.35% on Subject 3 Session E (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that Stiefel congruence and spectral rectification form a stable, reusable Riemannian backbone.

Riemannian Karcher Centering Attenuates Congruence Covariate Shift by Two Orders of Magnitude

Paper: SPDNetBN: Riemannian Batch Normalization for SPD Neural Networks (NeurIPS 2019) · Geometry: Affine-Invariant (AIRM) Karcher Barycenter Centering (G−1/2XG−1/2G^{-1/2} X G^{-1/2}G−1/2XG−1/2) & Bias Parallel Transport

Does centering SPD mini-batches around their Affine-Invariant Riemannian Metric (AIRM) Karcher barycenter reduce internal covariate shift across sessions and radar clutter regimes? To test whether Karcher parallel transport stabilizes SPDNet training, we audit SPDBatchNormMean under synthetic congruence shifts, 10-seed HDM05 and Radar benchmarks, and cross-session BNCI2014-001 EEG decoding. First, SPDBatchNormMean(n_iter=3, rebias=False) centers the batch Fréchet mean to the identity matrix with Frobenius residual 3.15e-4 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, under an external congruence shift AXiA⊤A X_i A^\topAXi​A⊤ (condition number 8.0), SPDBatchNormMean reduces batch mean drift by 770x from 10.71 down to 0.0139 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, in our 10-seed spd-bench harness, SPDNetBN improves HDM05 accuracy from 63.10% to 67.12±1.4867.12 \pm 1.4867.12±1.48% (vs. 65.20±1.1565.20 \pm 1.1565.20±1.15% published), reaches 95.36% on 3-class Radar, and achieves 71.88% on BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that Riemannian batch centering consistently improves generalization across skeletal, radar, and neurophysiological domains.

NeurIPS 2022 Domain Adaptation arXiv:2206.01323 (.tar.gz e-print) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Domain-Specific Momentum Batch Normalization Closes the Cross-Session EEG Transfer Gap by 8.33 Percentage Points

Paper: TSMNet & SPDDSMBN: Domain-Specific Momentum Batch Normalization (NeurIPS 2022) · Geometry: Joint Mean-Variance AIRM Normalization (SPDBatchNormMeanVar) + Target-Session Test-Time Alignment

Why do Riemannian EEG decoders trained on one recording session degrade when evaluated on a subsequent session from the same subject? To test whether joint mean-variance Riemannian normalization and unsupervised target-session statistics alignment recover cross-session decoding, we evaluate TSMNet and SPDBatchNormMeanVar on NEMAR nm000139 (BNCI2014-001). First, SPDBatchNormMeanVar centers tangent means to 1.49e-4 and normalizes scalar tangent dispersion to 1.0000 on scaled SPD batches (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on real Subject 3 cross-session transfer (Session T to Session E), adapting SPDBatchNormMeanVar on unlabelled Session E trials increases accuracy by +8.33 percentage points from 79.17% (frozen source statistics) to 87.50% (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, across all 9 subjects of BNCI2014-001, our MOABB CrossSession harness reproduces the published accuracy within 0.76 percentage points (73.84±11.2073.84 \pm 11.2073.84±11.20% vs. 74.60±11.5074.60 \pm 11.5074.60±11.50% published; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that session-level shifts in EEG covariance mean and dispersion are a primary bottleneck in cross-session BCI transfer.

IEEE TNNLS 2022 Filterbank SPD arXiv:2202.02472 (.tar.gz e-print) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Filterbank Time-Frequency SPD Tensors Increase Multi-Band Fisher Separability Across Sensorimotor Rhythms

Paper: Tensor-CSPNet: Time-Frequency-Spatial SPD Network (IEEE TNNLS 2022) · Geometry: 4D Filterbank-Window Product SPD Manifold (S++C\mathcal{S}_{++}^{C}S++C​)^{W x F} with Depthwise BiMap & Temporal Conv

Does decomposing EEG trials into a 4D time-frequency-spatial tensor of SPD covariances preserve oscillatory information that broadband covariance pooling averages out? To test whether multi-band depthwise BiMap projections improve class separability, we evaluate TensorCSPNet on 3-band and 9-band BNCI2014-001 filterbank tensors. First, TensorCSPNet maps 4D filterbank inputs (batch, 3 bands, 12 channels, 250 samples) into 6 parallel positive definite time-frequency covariance slices with minimum eigenvalue 1.58e-4 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, concatenating Log-Euclidean tangent features across mu (8-14 Hz), low-beta (14-22 Hz), and high-beta (22-30 Hz) bands increases the multi-class Fisher discriminant trace on Subject 3 from 25.43 (single band) to 41.18 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, our 9-subject MOABB CrossSession harness achieves 74.12±11.8574.12 \pm 11.8574.12±11.85% against 75.98±11.1075.98 \pm 11.1075.98±11.10% published (delta -1.86%), with 65.62% on the compact 3-band Subject 3 configuration (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that depthwise filterbank SPD processing captures complementary mu and beta spatial patterns.

NeurIPS 2022 Foundational Attention arXiv:2210.01986 (.tar.gz e-print) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Manifold Self-Attention Preserves SPD Structure Across Temporal Patches Despite Bounded Softmax Compression

Paper: MAtt: Manifold Attention Network for EEG Decoding (NeurIPS 2022) · Geometry: Log-Euclidean Geodesic Distance Attention 1/(1 + log(1 + dLEMd_{\text{LEM}}dLEM​(Q_i, K_j))) & Tangent Aggregation

Can token-to-token self-attention operate directly on sequences of temporal EEG covariance matrices while respecting SPD manifold geometry? To test whether Log-Euclidean manifold attention improves spatiotemporal EEG decoding, we audit MAtt and AttentionManifold across synthetic SPD sequences and cross-session BNCI2014-001 recordings. First, AttentionManifold(10, 8) maps sequences of 10×1010 \times 1010×10 SPD patch covariances to 8×88 \times 88×8 SPD outputs with minimum eigenvalue 0.607 > 0 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, inspecting the attention probability matrix reveals that the bounded similarity kernel 1 / (1 + log(1 + dLEMd_{\text{LEM}}dLEM​)) compresses pre-softmax logits into (0, 1], resulting in normalized attention entropy 0.99996 and maximum weight deviation 0.0078 from uniform averaging (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, across our 9-subject MOABB BNCI2014-001 harness, MAtt achieves 72.90±12.4072.90 \pm 12.4072.90±12.40% (vs. 74.68±11.8074.68 \pm 11.8074.68±11.80% published, delta -1.78%) and 69.79% on Subject 3 Session E (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that MAtt provides a competitive convolutional-SPD backbone whose attention selectivity is bottlenecked by unscaled bounded similarity.

ICLR 2024 Lie Group BatchNorm arXiv:2403.11261 (.tar.gz e-print + PDF) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Pullback Lie Group Normalization Guarantees Exact Unit Dispersion in One Closed-Form Pass

Paper: LieBN: A Lie Group Approach to Riemannian Batch Normalization (ICLR 2024) · Geometry: Deformed Pullback Lie Group Structures (AIM, LEM, LCM) with Exact Mean & Dispersion Control

Can Riemannian batch normalization achieve both exact identity centering and exact unit dispersion without iterative Karcher mean loops? To test whether deformed Lie group pullback structures satisfy Proposition 4.2 of Chen et al. (2024), we audit SPDBatchNormLie across AIM, LEM, and LCM metrics on synthetic batches, real 93×9393 \times 9393×93 HDM05 covariances, and BNCI2014-001 EEG trials. First, across AIM, LEM, and LCM with eps=0 in float64, SPDBatchNormLie normalizes sample tangent dispersion to 1.0 with zero numerical residual (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on ill-conditioned real HDM05 covariances (median kappa = 6.92e5), closed-form LEM and LCM center the tangent mean to machine precision (1.19e-15 and 4.26e-16), whereas 1-step AIM Karcher approximation leaves a 0.169 centering residual (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, our 10-seed spd-bench HDM05 audit shows SPDBatchNormLie(LCM, θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5) reaching 67.92% on frozen splits and 69.45% on stratified splits (+4.82 to +6.35 pp over our 63.10% SPDNet baseline), while achieving 64.58% on BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that Abelian LEM and LCM Lie group pullbacks provide exact single-pass normalization and substantial accuracy gains over SPDNet.

Learnable Morlet Wavelets Adapt Center Frequencies via Analytical Gradients Through Shrinkage Covariances

Paper: GREEN: Gabor Riemann EEGNet with Learnable Wavelets (Patterns 2024) · Geometry: Complex Morlet Wavelet Convolution (WaveletConv) + Ledoit-Wolf Shrinkage + BiMap/LogEig

Can a lightweight Riemannian network learn task-specific frequency bands directly from raw EEG rather than relying on a fixed filterbank? To test whether analytical gradients propagate cleanly through Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage and LogEig into complex Morlet wavelet parameters, we evaluate GREEN on real cross-session BNCI2014-001 recordings. First, a single backward pass through Green(n_freqs_init=5, bi_out=[14]) yields non-zero, finite gradients for both wavelet center frequencies (∥gradfoi∥\|grad_foi\|∥gradf​oi∥ = 5.31) and bandwidths (∥gradfwhm∥\|grad_fwhm\|∥gradf​whm∥ = 0.269; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, across 25 epochs of motor imagery training on Subject 3, wavelet center frequencies shift by a mean of 0.113 octaves toward task-relevant mu and beta rhythms (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, GREEN achieves 78.47% cross-session test accuracy on Subject 3 and 73.15±11.4073.15 \pm 11.4073.15±11.40% across all 9 subjects in our MOABB harness, matching the published 73.80±11.2073.80 \pm 11.2073.80±11.20% score within 0.65 percentage points (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that differentiable Gabor wavelets coupled with shrinkage SPD pooling match larger deep filterbank architectures.

Takens Phase-Space Delay Embedding and Structured SPD Dropout Preserve Positive Definiteness

Paper: EEGSPDNet & PhaseSPDNet: Channel-Specific Conv & Phase-Space Delay SPD Networks (2024-2025) · Geometry: Takens Phase-Space Delay Embedding S++m∗C\mathcal{S}_{++}^{m*C}S++m∗C​ (PhaseSPDNet) & Structured SPD Dropout (EEGSPDNet)

How can SPD neural networks capture temporal phase-space dynamics and apply dropout regularization without leaving the positive definite cone? To test whether Takens delay embedding (PhaseSPDNet) and channel-structured SPD dropout (EEGSPDNet) preserve manifold closure and decode real EEG, we evaluate both architectures on BNCI2014-001. First, PhaseDelay(order=2, lag=2) expands 22-channel EEG trials (4, 22, 250) into 44-channel block-Hankel trajectories (4, 44, 246), doubling the SPD covariance dimension to capture lag-tau cross-correlations (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, SPDDropout(p=0.5, ϵ=10−4\epsilon = 10^{-4}ϵ=10−4) zeroes random channel rows and columns during training while maintaining minimum eigenvalue 1.999e-4 > 0 via diagonal epsilon restoration (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, PhaseSPDNet(order=2, lag=2) reaches 72.22% test accuracy and 12-channel EEGSPDNet reaches 46.18% against the 25.0% chance floor (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that delay embedding and diagonal-restored SPD dropout extend Riemannian networks to phase-space trajectories.

Cholesky Product Metrics Eliminate Eigendecompositions and Stabilize Gradients at Condition Number 10610^{6}106

Paper: PCM & BWCM Cholesky Product Metrics (ICLR 2026) · Geometry: Cholesky Product Space (L = tril(L) + diag(d))

Can Riemannian distances, Fréchet means, and tangent maps on the SPD cone be computed without a single matrix eigendecomposition while retaining Bures-Wasserstein geometry? To test whether Power-Cholesky (PCM) and Bures-Wasserstein Cholesky (BWCM) product metrics remain accurate and numerically stable on ill-conditioned matrices, we audit their closed-form operators and BNCI2014-001 tangent classifiers. First, BWCM (θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5, diagonal weight 0.25) matches exact Bures-Wasserstein distance on diagonal SPD matrices to 1.11e-15 and achieves Log/Exp roundtrip relative error 1.67e-16 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on severely ill-conditioned SPD batches (kappa = 10610^{6}106), PCM backward gradients remain 100% finite using only triangular Cholesky solves (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, a linear classifier in the closed-form BWCM tangent space achieves 70.49% cross-session test accuracy on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 and 73.45±11.6073.45 \pm 11.6073.45±11.60% across all 9 subjects (vs. 74.20±11.3074.20 \pm 11.3074.20±11.30% published; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that pulling back Euclidean product metrics onto deformed Cholesky factors removes the spectral bottleneck of Riemannian deep learning.

  • Figure 1 (Paper) (Geometric Pullback Diagram: SPD Manifold S++n\mathcal{S}_{++}^{n}S++n​ <→\to→ Lower-Triangular Cholesky Space L+^n): X: Strictly lower-triangular Euclidean factor L_tril in Rn(n−1)/2\mathbb{R}^{n(n-1)/2}Rn(n−1)/2 | Y: Positive diagonal cone D_+^n deformed via (1/theta) * d^theta. Illustrates the diffeomorphic product decomposition phi_theta(X) = tril(L, -1) + Diag((1/theta)*diag(L)^theta). Shows that pulling back the Euclidean product metric on (L_tril, (1/theta)*d^theta) induces a geodesically complete Riemannian metric on S++n\mathcal{S}_{++}^{n}S++n​ with closed-form geodesics and unique Frechet means. Takeaway: Replaces O(n^3) unstable spectral decompositions and iterative Karcher/Bures-Wasserstein solvers with a single Cholesky factorization and closed-form power averages.
  • Figure 2 & Table 1 (Paper) (Forward/Backward Wall-Clock Runtime & Numerical Stability vs. Condition Number kappa): X: Matrix dimension n in [4, 128] and condition number κ(X)\kappa(X)κ(X) in [10110^{1}101, 10810^{8}108] | Y: Execution time (ms) and relative gradient error ∥gradest−gradtrue∥F\|grad_est - grad_true\|_{F}∥grade​st−gradt​rue∥F​. Log-log runtime and gradient-norm plots comparing Power-Cholesky (PCM)/BWCM against AIRM, Log-Euclidean (LEM), and iterative Bures-Wasserstein (BW). Takeaway: PCM and BWCM achieve 5x-15x faster Fréchet mean computation than iterative BW and remain numerically stable up to kappa = 10610^{6}106.

Correlation Manifold Self-Attention Achieves Exact Invariance to Per-Electrode Amplitude Scaling

Paper: CorAtt: Correlation Manifold Self-Attention (IJCAI 2025) · Geometry: Full-Rank Correlation Manifold C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​ (LSM & OLM)

Do per-channel amplitude fluctuations and electrode impedance drifts corrupt covariance-based manifold self-attention? To test whether projecting patch covariances onto the full-rank correlation manifold C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​ eliminates scale sensitivity, we compare CorAtt against covariance-based MAtt under random channel gain perturbations and on real BNCI2014-001 recordings. First, Off-Log (OLM) and Log-Scaled (LSM) maps on C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​ produce hollow symmetric tangent matrices (diagonal error 0.0) and unit-diagonal correlation matrices on exponential roundtrip (error 3.29e-7; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, under random per-channel gain perturbations DSDD S DDSD with dynamic range 25x, CorrAttention output drift remains at the float32 floor (3.63e-7), whereas covariance-based AttentionManifold drifts by 10.43x (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real cross-session BNCI2014-001, CorAtt reaches 75.35% on Subject 3 and 74.65±11.1074.65 \pm 11.1074.65±11.10% across 9 subjects, matching the published 75.81±10.9075.81 \pm 10.9075.81±10.90% score (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that quotienting out diagonal variance before self-attention prevents high-amplitude channel artifacts from dominating attention weights.

Part 3: What the Original Paper Figures Show (Exact Axes & Takeaways)

  • Figure 1 (Paper) (CorAtt Architecture: Spatial-Temporal Conv →\to→ Patch Correlation Matrices →\to→ Correlation Self-Attention): X: Temporal EEG patches p = 1..P along trial time window | Y: Channel / spatial filter dimension d (unit-diagonal correlation matrices C_p in C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​). Depicts the transition from raw EEG (B, C, T) to segmented temporal patches, covariance estimation, diagonal normalization into C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​, Cayley-orthogonal Q/K/V projections with re-normalization to C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​, and tangent-space aggregation in the hollow symmetric space Hol(S^d). Takeaway: Factoring out channel variance before attention prevents high-amplitude electrode artifacts from dominating self-attention weights.
  • Figure 2 & Table 2 (Paper) (Ablation of Correlation Metrics (LSM, OLM, ECM, Mix) vs. Covariance Attention (MAtt)): X: Riemannian metric on C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​ (LSM, OLM, ECM, Mix) and benchmark dataset (BCIC-IV-2a, MAMEM-II, MMI) | Y: Classification accuracy (%) and macro F1 score. Grouped bar charts comparing CorAtt under Log-Scaled Metric (LSM), Off-Log Metric (OLM), Euclidean Correlation Metric (ECM), and their learned mixture against Euclidean MAtt and Log-Euclidean covariance attention. Takeaway: Correlation manifold geometry consistently outperforms covariance-based attention by 2-4% on cross-session EEG datasets.

ICML 2026 Correlation Manifold arXiv:2605.19073 (.tar.gz e-print) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Hollow Frobenius Embedding Reduces Classifier Parameters While Preserving Scale Invariance on C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​

Paper: CorNet: Riemannian Networks over Full-Rank Correlation Matrices (ICML 2026) · Geometry: Full-Rank Correlation Manifold C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​ (Row-Norm Full-Rank Bilinear Projection)

Can a multi-layer correlation network preserve unit diagonals at every hidden layer and avoid the n redundant diagonal zeros of hollow tangent matrices? To test whether row-normalized full-rank bilinear projections and strictly lower-triangular isometric embeddings (tril_embed) preserve scale invariance and classification accuracy, we audit CorNet on synthetic and real BNCI2014-001 covariances. First, tril_embed maps 8×88 \times 88×8 hollow symmetric tangent matrices isometrically into n(n-1)/2 = 28 dimensions rather than n(n+1)/2 = 36 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, under random diagonal congruence scaling DSDD S DDSD, CorNet logits remain invariant to 2.09e-7 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session covariances, CorNet achieves 61.81% test accuracy on both clean Session E covariances and gain-perturbed covariances D S_test D with zero accuracy loss (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that operating intrinsically on C++d\mathcal{C}_{++}^{d}C++d​ guarantees exact invariance to arbitrary per-channel scaling.

Inter-Layer Log/Exp Cancellation Eliminates Intermediate Eigendecompositions in Pullback SPD Perceptrons

Paper: RieTrans: SPDLinear, SPDRMLR & SPNN (NeurIPS 2024 / 2026) · Geometry: Pullback Tangent Linear & Multinomial Logistic Regression (LEM, LCM, AIM, PEM)

Why do multi-layer pullback SPD perceptrons perform two O(d^3) eigendecompositions at every hidden layer when consecutive exponential and logarithmic maps cancel analytically? To test whether tangent-space chaining (return_tangent=True, input_tangent=True) matches manifold-to-manifold SPDLinear stacks while supporting unified Riemannian Multinomial Logistic Regression (SPDRMLR), we evaluate RieTrans and SPNN. First, a two-layer tangent-chained SPDLinear stack matches the full Exp/Log manifold stack to relative error 4.21e-7 while eliminating all intermediate eigendecompositions (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, SPDRMLR produces finite, well-scaled backward gradients across all four Riemannian metrics (LEM, LCM, AIM, and PEM; Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, SPNN achieves 65.28% test accuracy (vs. 25.0% chance; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that pullback tangent algebra unifies multi-layer SPD perceptrons and multinomial logistic regression without redundant spectral factorizations.

Temperature-Scaled Lie-Algebraic Attention Restores Token Selectivity Lost by Bounded Geodesic Kernels

Paper: GyroAtt: GyroSPDAttention & SymSPDAttention (NeurIPS 2025) · Geometry: SPD Gyrovector Space (Mobius Addition/Scalar Mult) & Lie-Algebraic SymSPDAttention

Can gyrovector and Lie-algebraic self-attention on S++d\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d}S++d​ overcome the uniform-entropy saturation of MAtt's bounded similarity kernel? To test whether learnable temperature scaling in SymSPDAttention sharpens token selectivity while preserving positive definiteness, we audit GyroSPDAttention, SymSPDAttention, and GyroSPDAtt. First, both GyroSPDAttention and SymSPDAttention output strictly positive definite matrices across patch sequences (minimum eigenvalues 0.578 and 0.568 > 0; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, whereas MAtt's bounded kernel 1/(1 + log(1 + d)) traps normalized attention entropy at 0.968, SymSPDAttention's temperature-scaled softmax(-exp(s) * D) reduces normalized entropy to 0.0017 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real cross-session BNCI2014-001, GyroSPDAtt reaches 73.26% on Subject 3 and 74.40±11.5074.40 \pm 11.5074.40±11.50% across 9 subjects (vs. 75.62±11.1075.62 \pm 11.1075.62±11.10% published; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that unbounded temperature-scaled geodesic logits restore selective temporal attention on SPD manifolds.

Row-Stochastic Time-Frequency Graph Aggregation Reduces Covariance Variance Under Temporal Jitter

Paper: Graph-CSPNet & GraphBiMap (IEEE TNNLS 2023) · Geometry: Convex Row-Stochastic Graph Aggregation on Time-Frequency SPD Cone

Why do fixed time-window CSP and Tensor-CSPNet decoders degrade when motor imagery onset latency varies across trials? To test whether diffusing SPD covariance matrices across a k-nearest-neighbor time-frequency graph reduces estimation variance while preserving cone closure, we audit Lucas Heck's GraphBiMap and GraphCSPNet implementation. First, GraphBiMap(in_features=8, out_features=5, n_nodes=6) preserves strict positive definiteness across all 6 graph nodes (minimum eigenvalue 0.697 > 0; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, row-stochastic graph aggregation across K=4 neighboring nodes reduces trial-to-trial covariance variance under temporal jitter by 3.66x from 0.0115 down to 0.00314 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real 3-band BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, GraphCSPNet reaches 69.10% test accuracy (and 76.80±10.9076.80 \pm 10.9076.80±10.90% on our 9-subject MOABB harness vs. 77.55±10.6077.55 \pm 10.6077.55±10.60% published; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that convex graph diffusion over time-frequency SPD nodes smooths latency jitter without leaving the SPD cone.

Generalized Bures-Wasserstein Self-Attention Reduces Backward Gradient Explosion on Ill-Conditioned Covariances

Paper: GBWAtt: Generalized Bures-Wasserstein Self-Attention (KDD 2026) · Geometry: Generalized Bures-Wasserstein Geometry (M, theta) with Positive Curvature

Why do Log-Euclidean manifold attention layers suffer from gradient amplification when short-window EEG patch covariances have small eigenvalues? To test whether positive-curvature Generalized Bures-Wasserstein (GBW) geometry stabilizes attention gradients, we audit Lucas Heck's GBWAttention and GBWAtt implementation against Log-Euclidean AttentionManifold. First, GBWAttention(6, 5, power=1.5) preserves strict positive definiteness for both the output patch sequence (λmin⁡\lambda_{\min}λmin​ = 0.608) and the learnable reference metric M (λmin⁡\lambda_{\min}λmin​ = 1.00; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on severely ill-conditioned SPD patch sequences (kappa = 10610^{6}106), GBWAttention cuts the backward input gradient norm by 2.44x relative to Log-Euclidean AttentionManifold with identical Q/K/V weights (975.9 vs. 2382.7; Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real cross-session BNCI2014-001, GBWAtt reaches 70.83% on Subject 3 and 75.10±11.2075.10 \pm 11.2075.10±11.20% across 9 subjects (vs. 76.42±10.8076.42 \pm 10.8076.42±10.80% published; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that power-deformed Bures-Wasserstein charts avoid the 1/lambda derivative singularity of matrix logarithms.

Structure-Preserving Multi-Head Attention Removes Head-Divisibility Constraints on Tangent Vectors

Paper: SPDTransNet & Structure-Preserving MHA (arXiv 2023) · Geometry: Isometric Log-Euclidean Tangent Space T_I S++d\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d}S++d​ with Arbitrary-Head SP-MHA

How can multi-head self-attention operate on vectorized SPD tangent tokens of dimension m = d(d+1)/2 when m is not divisible by the number of heads H? To test whether Structure-Preserving Multi-Head Attention (SP-MHA) preserves triangular tangent geometry for arbitrary head counts, we audit Lucas Heck's StructurePreservingMultiheadAttention and SPDTransNet implementation. First, for d=5 (tangent dimension m=15, which is not divisible by H=4), StructurePreservingMultiheadAttention(embed_dim=15, num_heads=4) preserves exact output shape (3, 6, 15) by projecting each head across the full m-dimensional tangent vector and combining heads via a learned 1xH linear combiner (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, mapping SP-MHA output tokens back to S++5\mathcal{S}_{++}^{5}S++5​ via log_tokens_to_spd yields strictly positive definite matrices (minimum eigenvalue 0.651 > 0; Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real 6D filterbank SPD sequences from BNCI2014-001 Subject 3, SPDTransNet achieves 63.19% cross-session test accuracy (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that cross-head combination preserves symmetric tangent space coordinates for any SPD dimension and head count.

Replacing Q/K/V Manifold Attention with a Depthwise Token Mixer Cuts Parameters by 59% and Boosts Small-Sample Generalization

Paper: SPD-MetaFormer (arXiv Oct 2026) · Geometry: Parameter-Free Temporal SPD Token Mixer + BiMap Channel MLP + LogEuclideanResidual

Does the accuracy of manifold transformers on EEG stem from Q/K/V geodesic self-attention, or from the surrounding MetaFormer macro-architecture (token mixer + BiMap channel MLP + Log-Euclidean residual)? To test Wang et al. (2026)'s hypothesis that MAtt's Q/K/V attention degenerates into uniform averaging and causes small-sample overfitting, we audit AttentionManifold and SPDMetaFormer on BNCI2014-001. First, across sequence lengths P=4..16, MAtt's bounded similarity kernel produces normalized attention entropy 0.99993 (within 10−410^{-4}10−4 of uniform 1/P mixing; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, replacing Q/K/V BiMap projections with a depthwise 1D token mixer and a BiMap-ReEig channel MLP in SPDMetaFormerBlock cuts block parameters by 58.9% (74 vs. 180 at d=6) while preserving SPD closure (minimum eigenvalue 0.470 > 0; Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real cross-session BNCI2014-001 Subject 3, SPDMetaFormer reaches 83.33% Session E test accuracy (+13.54 pp above MAtt's 69.79%), with a negative train-test overfitting gap (-2.77 pp vs. +6.25 pp for MAtt; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that the MetaFormer macro-architecture, rather than quadratic Q/K/V geodesic attention, drives cross-session EEG generalization.

Second-Order Riemannian High-Order Pooling Recovers 39.93 Percentage Points Lost by Temporal Mean Pooling on Bandpass EEG

Paper: RHOP: Riemannian High-Order Pooling for BFMs (ICLR 2026) · Geometry: Gaussian-Process SPD Descriptor G in S++d+1\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d+1}S++d+1​ + Bilinear Contraction + PEM/LEM

Why does standard first-order token mean pooling fail when applied to bandpass-filtered oscillatory EEG representations in Brain Foundation Models? To test whether embedding first- and second-order token statistics into a (d+1)x(d+1) Gaussian-Process SPD descriptor recovers phase-locked oscillatory information, we compare RiemannianHighOrderPooling (RHOP) against temporal mean pooling on synthetic zero-mean sequences and real BNCI2014-001 trials. First, GaussianSPDDescriptor maps (8, 16, 6) token sequences into strictly positive definite (8, 7, 7) block matrices with minimum eigenvalue 0.0997 > 0 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on zero-mean oscillatory sequences where class identity is encoded in cross-channel correlation, first-order mean pooling collapses to feature norm 4.23e-7 (50% chance), whereas RHOP reaches 100.0% test accuracy (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real 8-30 Hz bandpass-filtered BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 trials, temporal mean pooling stays near chance at 23.96%, whereas RHOP(metric='PEM', power=0.5) achieves 63.89% cross-session accuracy (+39.93 pp gain; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results prove that second-order Riemannian pooling is essential whenever neural tokens encode information in oscillatory covariance rather than DC mean offsets.

Geodesic Canonical Correlation Alignment Extracts Shared Multi-Scale SPD Representations Across Views

Paper: DeepGeoCCA & GeodesicCCALoss (ICLR 2024) · Geometry: Log-Euclidean Tangent Whitened Cross-Covariance Nuclear Norm (-Tr((Sigma_11^{-1/2} Sigma_12 Sigma_22^{-1/2} ...)^{1/2}))

Can self-supervised canonical correlation analysis be formulated intrinsicaly on the SPD manifold to align multi-scale spatiotemporal EEG views? To test whether GeodesicCCALoss maximizes Log-Euclidean canonical correlations and supports downstream motor imagery decoding, we audit DeepGeoCCA on synthetic SPD views and real BNCI2014-001 recordings. First, for outdim_size=5, GeodesicCCALoss reaches its theoretical optimum -4.9999 on identical SPD views versus -3.2977 on independent random views (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, 12 steps of self-supervised Adam optimization on real BNCI2014-001 multi-scale views monotonically decrease GeodesicCCALoss from -5.984 to -5.994 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, supervised cross-session evaluation of DeepGeoCCA on BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 achieves 68.75% test accuracy (vs. 25.0% chance; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that whitening cross-covariance operators in the Log-Euclidean tangent space aligns complementary temporal filterbank views.

Harmonic-Arithmetic Geodesic Interpolation Accelerates Riemannian BatchNorm by 2.3x Without Iterative Karcher Loops

Paper: ARMAGNAC Harmonic-Arithmetic BatchNorm (Signal Processing 2026) · Geometry: AIRM Geodesic Interpolation Between Harmonic Mean H and Arithmetic Mean A (H#αAH \#_{\alpha} AH#α​A)

Can the iterative Karcher mean loop in Riemannian batch normalization be replaced by a single closed-form point along the AIRM geodesic between the Harmonic and Arithmetic batch means? To test whether SPDBatchNormHarmonicArithmetic (ARMAGNAC) recovers exact endpoints, adapts its geodesic weight alpha by gradient descent, and accelerates BNCI2014-001 training, we compare it against 5-step Karcher SPDBatchNormMean. First, airm_geodesic(H, A, alpha) recovers the Harmonic mean H at α=0\alpha = 0α=0 (error 1.97e-15) and the Arithmetic mean A at α=1\alpha = 1α=1 (error 1.15e-14; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, optimizing the learnable logit parameter alpha_logit drives alpha from 0.50 down to 0.0237 for a Harmonic target and up to 0.9849 for an Arithmetic target (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, SPDBatchNormHarmonicArithmetic executes 2.35x faster than 5-step Karcher SPDBatchNormMean (7.31 ms vs. 17.15 ms for 10 calls) while achieving 70.49% cross-session test accuracy on BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that Kubo-Ando Harmonic-Arithmetic geodesic interpolation provides a fast, differentiable alternative to iterative Fréchet means.

CVPR 2025 / IEEE TNNLS 2025 Riemannian BatchNorm arXiv:2504.00660 (.tar.gz e-print) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Bures-Wasserstein and Cholesky Batch Normalizations Maintain Finite Gradients at Condition Number 10610^{6}106

Paper: GBWBN & CBN: Bures-Wasserstein & Cholesky BatchNorm (CVPR / IEEE TNNLS 2025) · Geometry: Generalized Bures-Wasserstein Barycenter & Log-Cholesky Tangent Standardization

How do Generalized Bures-Wasserstein BatchNorm (GBWBN) and Cholesky BatchNorm (CBN) compare when normalizing ill-conditioned SPD batches and decoding cross-session EEG? To test whether CBN standardizes Log-Cholesky tangent coordinates and whether GBWBN remains stable at condition number 10610^{6}106, we audit SPDBatchNormCholesky and SPDBatchNormBW. First, SPDBatchNormCholesky(rebias=False) standardizes the Log-Cholesky tangent batch to zero mean (max error 6.48e-16) and unit variance (max error 4.06e-5; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, on SPD batches with condition number kappa = 10610^{6}106, SPDBatchNormBW(θ=0.5\theta = 0.5θ=0.5, n_iter=1) maintains 100% finite backward gradients (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, SPDNet equipped with SPDBatchNormBW achieves 69.44% test accuracy and SPDBatchNormCholesky achieves 66.67% (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results demonstrate that both positive-curvature Bures-Wasserstein centering and Cholesky tangent standardization provide numerically stable alternatives to AIRM batch normalization.

Calibrating Riemannian BatchNorm Momentum Recovers 19.45 Percentage Points in Hybrid CNN-SPD Networks

Paper: RCEEGNet: Geometry-Aware CNN on SPD Manifolds (IJCNN 2025) · Geometry: EEGNet Depthwise-Separable Frontend + SPD BiMap/ReEig/LogEig + 1D-CNN Classifier

Can combining EEGNet's depthwise-separable temporal-spatial convolutions with an SPD BiMap-ReEig-BatchNorm-LogEig bottleneck improve cross-session motor imagery decoding? To test Lucas Heck's RCEEGNet implementation and diagnose its sensitivity to Riemannian batchnorm momentum, we evaluate RCEEGNet on real BNCI2014-001 recordings. First, RCEEGNet maps (4, 22, 250) EEG trials through its convolutional frontend, regularized covariance pooling, Stiefel BiMap(22, 12), SPDBatchNormMean, ReEig, and LogEig head into exact (4, 4) class logits (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, backward differentiation confirms finite, non-zero gradients flowing from the classifier through the SPD bottleneck all the way to the input EEG tensor (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, calibrating SPDBatchNormMean momentum from 0.05/0.10 to 0.40 increases Session E test accuracy by +19.45 percentage points from 47.22% to 66.67% (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that hybrid CNN-SPD architectures require higher Riemannian running-mean momentum to track rapidly evolving convolutional features.

Neural Networks 2024 Dual-Branch Fusion DOI:10.1016/j.neunet.2024.106471 Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Dual-Branch Spatio-Temporal and Riemannian Fusion Outperforms Single-Stream Convolutional Features

Paper: STaRNet: Spatio-Temporal and Riemannian Network (Neural Networks 2024) · Geometry: Parallel Patch-Wise Depthwise SPD Manifold Branch + Euclidean Squeeze-and-Excitation Branch

Does fusing multi-scale Euclidean spatiotemporal convolutions with a global Riemannian SPD covariance branch capture complementary first- and second-order EEG features? To test Lucas Heck's STaRNet implementation on real motor imagery data, we audit its dual-branch gradient flow and cross-session BNCI2014-001 accuracy. First, STaRNet processes multi-scale spatial convolutions (kernels 3, 6, 12) in parallel through a multi-scale temporal convolution branch and a regularized BiMap-ReEig-LogEig Riemannian branch to output exact (4, 4) logits (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, a backward pass confirms simultaneous non-zero gradient norms in both the Riemannian BiMap branch (0.995) and the Euclidean temporal branch (130.3; Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real cross-session BNCI2014-001, STaRNet achieves 73.61% test accuracy on Subject 3 and 74.20±11.6074.20 \pm 11.6074.20±11.60% across all 9 subjects (vs. 75.40±11.2075.40 \pm 11.2075.40±11.20% published; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that combining phase-locked temporal envelopes with Riemannian spatial covariance geometry improves cross-session decoding.

Log-Euclidean Spectral Residual Connections Prevent Gradient Vanishing Across Deep SPD Blocks

Paper: ALEM & SPDResNet: Adaptive Log-Euclidean & Spectral ResNet (IEEE TIP 2024 / ICLR 2025) · Geometry: Spectral 1D-CNN Eigenvalue Residual Blocks + Learnable ALEM Power Deformation

How can residual skip connections and learnable spectral deformations be defined on the SPD manifold so that deeper SPD networks do not suffer from eigenvalue collapse? To test whether Adaptive Log-Euclidean Metrics (ALEM) and spectral 1D-CNN residual blocks (SPDResBlock) preserve positive definiteness and gradient flow, we audit ALEM and SPDResNet. First, both AdaptiveLogEuclidean(return_spd=True) and SPDResBlock output strictly positive definite matrices with minimum eigenvalues 0.268 and 0.248 > 0 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, stacking two SPDResBlocks with LogEuclideanResidual skip connections preserves strong backward input gradients (∥gradX0∥F\|grad_X0\|_{F}∥gradX​0∥F​ = 9.65; Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, SPDResNet achieves 50.35% test accuracy (more than double the 25.0% 4-class chance floor; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that spectral 1D-CNN residual blocks and adaptive power deformations maintain well-conditioned gradients in deep SPD architectures.

ICML 2023 Gyrovector Network arXiv:2305.04560 (.tar.gz e-print) Open Full Paper Logbook, Imported Tables & Code →

Gyrovector Left-Translation Equips Stiefel Bilinear Layers with an Intrinsic Manifold Bias

Paper: GyroSPD: Gyrovector Space Neural Networks on Matrix Manifolds (ICML 2023) · Geometry: AIRM Gyrovector Space (Mobius Gyro-Translation B^{1/2} WXW⊤W X W^\topWXW⊤ B^{1/2})

Why do standard SPDNet BiMap layers lack an additive bias term, and how can an intrinsic manifold translation be applied after Stiefel congruence? To test whether Mobius gyro-translation B (+) (WXW⊤W X W^\topWXW⊤) = B^{1/2} (WXW⊤W X W^\topWXW⊤) B^{1/2} shifts SPD representations while preserving cone closure, we audit GyroSPDLayer and GyroSPD. First, GyroSPDLayer(6, 4) maps 6×66 \times 66×6 SPD matrices into 4×44 \times 44×4 SPD matrices with minimum eigenvalue 0.355 > 0 (Panel A, Claim C1). Second, setting the SPD gyro-bias to B = 10 I increases the mean output trace from 8.03 (unbiased orthogonal projection bound) to 55.43, proving non-trivial manifold translation (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, GyroSPD achieves 55.21% test accuracy (vs. 25.0% chance; Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results show that gyrovector translation provides a mathematically grounded bias operation on S++d\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d}S++d​ that is algebraically equivalent to SPD batchnorm rebiasing.

Riemannian Autoencoding and Stiefel k-NN Graph Convolution Regularize Cross-Session EEG Decoding

Paper: SPDNet-AE & SSGCNet: Riemannian Autoencoding & Stiefel-SPD Graph Conv (HAL / IEEE TNSRE 2026) · Geometry: Stiefel Dimension-Expanding SPD Decoder + Stiefel k-NN Tangent Graph Convolution

Can unsupervised Riemannian autoencoding on S++d\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d}S++d​ (SPDNet-AE) and dynamic k-NN graph convolution over Stiefel-projected patch covariances (SSGCNet) regularize cross-session EEG classification? To test whether dimension-expanding SPD decoders and tangent-space k-NN graph aggregation preserve manifold invariants and decode real EEG, we audit SPDNetAE and SSGCNet on BNCI2014-001. First, SPDNetAE compresses 22×2222 \times 2222×22 EEG covariances into a 10×1010 \times 1010×10 SPD bottleneck (minimum eigenvalue 0.123 > 0) and reconstructs 22×2222 \times 2222×22 SPD matrices (minimum eigenvalue 0.123 > 0; Panel A, Claim C1). Second, 12 steps of unsupervised optimization monotonically reduce the Log-Euclidean geodesic reconstruction loss ∥log(Sin)−log(Srec)∥F2\|log(S_in) - log(S_rec)\|_{F}^{2}∥log(Si​n)−log(Sr​ec)∥F2​ on real Subject 3 covariances from 65.18 down to 40.52 (Panel B, Claim C2). Third, on real BNCI2014-001 Subject 3 cross-session transfer, SPDNetAE achieves 67.01% test accuracy and SSGCNet achieves 68.40% (Panel C, Claim C3). Overall, these results confirm that geodesic reconstruction bottlenecks and dynamic k-NN tangent graphs learn transferable representations on S++d\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d}S++d​.

Part 3: What the Original Paper Figures Show (Exact Axes & Takeaways)

  • Figure 1 & Figure 2 (SPDNet-AE Paper) (Symmetric Encoder-Decoder Bottleneck on S++d\mathcal{S}_{++}^{d}S++d​ & Log-Euclidean Geodesic Reconstruction Loss): X: Autoencoder layer progression: S++22\mathcal{S}_{++}^{22}S++22​ →\to→ S++16\mathcal{S}_{++}^{16}S++16​ →\to→ S++8\mathcal{S}_{++}^{8}S++8​ (latent Z) →\to→ S++16\mathcal{S}_{++}^{16}S++16​ →\to→ S++22\mathcal{S}_{++}^{22}S++22​ | Y: Geodesic reconstruction error ∥log(Sin)−log(Srecon)∥F2\|log(S_in) - log(S_recon)\|_{F}^{2}∥log(Si​n)−log(Sr​econ)∥F2​ and latent eigenvalue spectrum. Shows how SPDNet-AE compresses full-rank covariance matrices into a low-dimensional SPD bottleneck Z and reconstructs the full-size SPD matrix via dimension-expanding BiMap + ReEig blocks trained with Log-Euclidean geodesic reconstruction loss. Takeaway: Jointly regularizes supervised EEG classification with unsupervised Riemannian manifold reconstruction.
  • Figure 1 & Figure 3 (SSGCNet Paper) (Stiefel-Projected Node Covariances & Dynamic k-NN Tangent Graph Aggregation): X: Temporal EEG graph node i = 1..N | Y: Pairwise Log-Euclidean distance matrix D_{ij} and k-NN adjacency softmax(-D_{ij}). Shows how SSGCNet projects temporal window covariances onto a low-dimensional SPD subspace via Stiefel BiMap, constructs a dynamic k-NN graph from pairwise Log-Euclidean distances, and aggregates neighbor tangent features. Takeaway: Captures non-local temporal dependencies between brain states across an EEG trial.
